question: How does the `next-async-request-api` codemod transform a Client Component (`'use client'`) that synchronously reads `params.slug`?
options: It marks the Client Component as `async` and inserts `await props.params` at the top of the function
It removes `'use client'` so the component becomes an async Server Component automatically
It wraps the `params` prop type in `Promise<...>` and unwraps it using `React.use(props.params)`
explanation: Because Client Components cannot be `async` functions, the codemod updates the prop type to `Promise<...>` and unwraps the Promise inside the component using React's `use()` hook.

question: What does the `next-async-request-api` codemod do when it finds `cookies().get('token')` inside a synchronous utility function that cannot be automatically converted to `async`?
options: It deletes the utility function and inlines the cookie read into every file in the project
It inserts a `@next-codemod-error` comment and casts the call to `UnsafeUnwrappedCookies` so developers can refactor the call chain to `async`
It rewrites the utility function to read `document.cookie` instead of `next/headers`
It aborts the entire codemod run without modifying any files in the repository
explanation: When a non-component synchronous helper calls `cookies()` or `headers()`, the codemod flags the call site with `@next-codemod-error` and `UnsafeUnwrappedCookies` so you can manually make the helper and its callers `async`.

question: What is the purpose of running `npx next typegen` in a Next.js TypeScript project?
options: It compiles all Server Components into WebAssembly modules before `next dev` starts
It generates route-aware TypeScript definitions (`PageProps`, `LayoutProps`, `RouteContext`) based on your `app/` directory structure without running a full build
It automatically converts all `.js` files in the project to `.tsx` files
It generates database schema types for Prisma and Drizzle from `cookies()` calls
explanation: `npx next typegen` inspects your `app/` routes and generates `.next/types` definitions—including `PageProps` and `LayoutProps` with strongly typed `Promise` `params`—so `tsc --noEmit` can validate route types standalone.

question: When using `PageProps<'/[org]/repos/[repo]'>` generated by `next typegen`, what is the TypeScript type of `props.params`?
explanation: `PageProps` and `LayoutProps` generated by `next typegen` type `params` as a `Promise` resolving to an object whose keys exactly match the dynamic route segments in the route path.
